newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close down after resources fade.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close down after resources fade.

text.p: Australian shares closed slightly weaker on Monday after a bout of selling in the resources sector in the last hour of trading.
The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, closed 1.1 points lower at 2,334.1, well off its intra-day high of 2,346.9.
The December share price index ended down three points at 2,342 and at a 7.9 point premium to the underlying index.
Dealers said turnover was noticeably thin with investors cautious after the market's sharp sell-off on Friday and ahead of important U.S. economic data due out later this week.
"The market was quiet all day," a dealer at a Brisbane-based brokerage said.
"Investors that were in early wanted to be fairly square at the end of the day because Wall Street could be a volatile animal this week," he said.
The dealer said industrial issues were supported by a stronger bond market which was still confident that a local monetary easing was a near term prospect.

"Investors remain comfortable with the relatively high level of the Australian market but are less secure with a Dow above 6,000. The fear is the U.S. market has been over-inflated by the presidential election," the dealer said.
The bank sector outperformed the market on the day and ANZ stock was active after the company denied it was discussing merger plans with U.K. bank Standard Chartered.
ANZ shares ended four cents firmer at A$7.20 (US$5.69) on turnover of 1.7 million shares.

Another strong performer was nickel hopeful Anaconda Nickel whose shares went for a run after the company announced it had placed stock with its major shareholder, Swiss commodities group, Glencore International AG.
Anaconda shares closed 22 cents higher at A$3.70, just 15 cents shy of their all-time high of A$3.85.
